items.question: How often does ModeAlert check for updates?
items.answer: Automatically, once a day — you never have to refresh a page or check a launcher yourself.

items.question: Which games are supported?
items.answer: {count} games today — League of Legends, Valorant, Destiny 2, TFT, Fortnite, Warframe, Path of Exile, Helldivers 2, Foxhole, PUBG, PlanetSide 2, Final Fantasy XIV, and EA Sports FC — with more added as new tracking sources come online.

items.question: Is ModeAlert free?
items.answer: Yes — the Free plan tracks up to 5 events with email and Discord alerts, no credit card required. Premium ($4.99/mo) adds unlimited tracked events and per-event predictions.

items.question: How do you detect events before Riot announces them?
items.answer: We compare live game data against Riot's public test environment (PBE), which usually receives new content days or weeks before it goes live — giving you the earliest signal available.

items.question: Do I need to install anything?
items.answer: No. ModeAlert is entirely web-based — no client, no browser extension, no background app.

items.question: How will I be notified?
items.answer: Email and Discord today (add a webhook URL in Settings). Telegram is on the roadmap.

featuresPage.title: Everything ModeAlert does, in one place.
featuresPage.introPre: ModeAlert exists to answer one question automatically:
featuresPage.introQuote: “did the game mode I care about just go live?”
featuresPage.introPost: Here's exactly how it does that.
featuresPage.pbeDescription: For League of Legends, we compare the live patch against Riot's Public Beta Environment — new modes and events often show up there days or weeks before they officially launch.
featuresPage.alertsDescription: Get a clean, readable email — or a message posted straight to your own Discord server via webhook — the moment your selected mode or event goes live, ends, or changes status. No dashboard-refreshing required.
featuresPage.gamesDescription: League of Legends, Valorant, Destiny 2, TFT, Fortnite, Warframe, Path of Exile, Helldivers 2, Foxhole, PUBG, PlanetSide 2, Final Fantasy XIV, and EA Sports FC — one watchlist instead of a different tracker, Discord bot, or community site per game.
featuresPage.dailyDescription: A scheduled sync checks every source once a day and diffs it against what it saw last time — new, changed, and ended events are detected without you doing anything.
featuresPage.watchDescription: Pick specific modes and events per game instead of getting notified about everything — URF, Arena, Night Market, battle passes, whatever you actually care about.
featuresPage.privacyDescription: We only store what's needed to send the alerts you asked for — your watchlist, your email, and a Discord webhook URL if you add one. No tracking pixels, no data resale.
featuresPage.whyTitle: Manually checking is the actual problem.
featuresPage.whyPara1: Limited-time modes disappear the same way they appear — with little warning. By the time a mode trends on social media, it might already be halfway through its run. Refreshing a patch notes page or a Twitter feed every day doesn't scale, and most players just miss things instead.
featuresPage.whyPara2: ModeAlert flips that: instead of you checking on the game, the game gets checked on your behalf, once a day, across every title you've set up. You only hear from us when something on your watchlist actually changes.
featuresPage.ctaIntro: Free to start. Set up your first alert in under a minute.

privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.whoWeAreBodyPost: ) is an independent, early-access project built and operated by Deniz Önen. This policy explains what data ModeAlert collects, why, and how you can remove it.
privacyPage.whatWeCollectIntro: ModeAlert only stores what it needs to run your watchlist and send the alerts you asked for:

collectItems.label: Account info
collectItems.body: your email address, and your name/profile image if you sign in with Google. If you sign in with a password instead, we store a salted hash of it, never the password itself.

collectItems.label: Watchlist
collectItems.body: the games and events you've chosen to track.

collectItems.label: Notification history
collectItems.body: a record of the alerts we've sent you, so you can review them in your dashboard.

collectItems.label: Session cookies
collectItems.body: used only to keep you signed in. No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies are set.

collectItems.label: Discord webhook URL
collectItems.body: only if you add one in Settings to get alerts posted to your own Discord server. You control that URL; removing it from Settings deletes it from our database.

collectItems.label: Subscription status
collectItems.body: if you upgrade to Premium, we store your plan, subscription status, and Lemon Squeezy's customer/subscription IDs (opaque references, not your card details) so we can grant access and let you manage billing.

collectItems.label: Product usage
collectItems.body: a small number of first-party events (e.g. finishing onboarding, hitting the free plan's limit) tied to your account, so we can see where the product is confusing without sending anything to a third party.

collectItems.label: Anonymous page views
collectItems.body: on the homepage and sign-up page only, we count that a page was viewed. No cookie, no visitor id, no IP address is stored with it — just a running total, so we can tell whether the homepage is actually leading anywhere. It can never be linked back to you or to any later account you create.

privacyPage.noThirdPartyTrackers: We don't use tracking pixels, third-party analytics scripts, or ad networks, and we don't sell or rent your data to anyone.
privacyPage.whoWeShareIntro: A small number of infrastructure providers process data on our behalf, strictly to run the service:
shareItems: **Neon** (Postgres database hosting) and **Vercel** (application hosting) — store and serve the data described above.
**Resend** — delivers the email alerts you sign up for.
**Discord** — only if you add a webhook URL in Settings, we send your event alerts directly to that URL. That's a channel you control on your own server, not a service we otherwise integrate with.
**Google** — only if you choose "Sign in with Google", to authenticate you.

**Lemon Squeezy** — only if you upgrade to Premium. They're our payment processor and Merchant of Record, so they handle your payment details directly (card number, billing address) — ModeAlert never sees or stores them. They notify us only of your subscription status.
privacyPage.publicApisNote: ModeAlert also calls public game-data APIs (Riot Games, Bungie, and others) to detect events, but no information about you personally is ever sent to them.
controlItems: Every email includes a one-click unsubscribe link — no account login required.
You can edit or clear your watchlist any time from your dashboard.
**Download your data** — Settings has a "Download my data" button that gives you a JSON file of your account, watchlist, and notification history, any time, no waiting on a request.
**Delete your account** — Settings also has a self-service "Delete account" button that removes your account and all associated data immediately, no email required.
privacyPage.changesBody: ModeAlert is an early-access, actively developed product. If this policy changes in a meaningful way, we'll update the date above and, where practical, notify active users by email.
privacyPage.contactBodyPre: Questions about this policy or your data? Email

termsPage.s1BodyPost: ) is an independent, early-access project, built and operated by Deniz Önen, that watches public data from game publishers and alerts you by email or Discord when a game mode or event you're tracking changes. By creating an account or using the site, you agree to these terms.

termsPage.s2Body: ModeAlert is an independent, unofficial tool. It is not endorsed by, affiliated with, or sponsored by Riot Games, Bungie, Epic Games, Digital Extremes, Grinding Gear Games, Arrowhead Game Studios, Siege Camp/Clapfoot, or any other publisher whose public data it reads. termsPage.s3Title: 3. Free and Premium plans — no guarantees
termsPage.s3Body: ModeAlert's Free plan is provided **as-is**, without warranty of any kind, and Premium doesn't change that. Event detection depends entirely on third-party APIs we don't control — they can change, rate-limit, or go offline without notice, which can delay or prevent an alert. We do our best to keep data accurate and timely, but we can't guarantee you'll be notified of every event, or that notifications will always be on time.
termsPage.s4Body: Premium is $4.99/month, billed monthly until you cancel. Payments are processed by **Lemon Squeezy**, our Merchant of Record — Lemon Squeezy handles your payment details directly and is the merchant on your card statement; ModeAlert never sees or stores your card number.
termsPage.s4Item1: You can cancel anytime from **Dashboard → Settings** — you keep Premium access until the end of the period you already paid for, then the account reverts to Free (your data isn't deleted, tracking above the Free limit just pauses).

You agree to use ModeAlert only for its intended purpose — tracking game events for yourself — and not to abuse, scrape, or overload the service.
We may suspend or remove accounts that abuse the service or violate these terms.
termsPage.s6Body: ModeAlert is actively developed and may change features, supported games, or pricing over time. Existing Free functionality won't be removed retroactively without reasonable notice.
termsPage.s7Body: To the extent permitted by law, ModeAlert and its operator aren't liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of, or inability to use, the service — including a missed or late notification about a game event.
termsPage.s8Body: We may update these terms as the product evolves. If a change is significant, we'll update the date above and, where practical, notify active users by email.

statisticsPage.title: Site-wide stats
statisticsPage.intro: Computed directly from real tracking history — no estimates or placeholder numbers. History tracking started 2026-08-04, so some numbers below will fill in as more events complete.
statisticsPage.popularityIntro: Real watchlist counts by game and category — how many people are actually tracking each kind of event, not an estimate.
statisticsPage.mostTrackedIntro: Events ranked by how many times we've seen them occur.
statisticsPage.mostTrackedEmpty: No history recorded yet — check back after the next sync.
statisticsPage.avgDurationIntro: Across every event that has fully completed (start to end) at least once.
statisticsPage.avgDurationEmpty: Not enough events have completed yet to compute this.
statisticsPage.predictionIntro: How close our end-time predictions land to what actually happened, tested retrospectively against real history.
statisticsPage.predictionEmpty: Not enough events have recurred and completed yet to score this.
statisticsPage.uptimeIntro: Share of sync attempts that succeeded per provider, last {days} days. Recorded on every sync — data starts filling in from 2026-08-06.
statisticsPage.uptimeEmpty: No health checks recorded yet — check back after the next sync.
statisticsPage.notificationsIntro: Every send attempt (success or failure, all channels) is recorded, so the success rate below is real, not just a count of what worked.
statisticsPage.noSendAttempts: No send attempts in the last 30 days.
statisticsPage.reportedWrongIntro: Real user reports — a recipient flagged a specific notification as inaccurate, not an inferred guess.

livePage.title: What's Happening Right Now?
livePage.intro: The current status of every tracked mode across every game — live, upcoming, tracking, or ended.
livePage.allGamesEmpty: No tracked modes right now — check back after the next sync.
livePage.cdragonTitle: Early Signal Detail for League of Legends
livePage.pbeTitle: On PBE But Not Live Yet (Early Signal)
livePage.pbeCheckFailed: The PBE check failed just now (the PBE server may be temporarily unreachable).
livePage.pbeEmpty: Nothing is on PBE that isn't already live. That's normal — CDragon's event-hub file mostly covers pre-planned content like season passes / battle passes.
livePage.urfTitle: URF Status — Why Isn't It Shown Here?
livePage.urfPara1Pre: URF (Ultra Rapid Fire) is always defined in CommunityDragon's
livePage.urfPara1Post: file — that's not an "active" signal, just "this queue type exists." Riot never publishes when URF is actually open in any public or datamined file ahead of time; they only announce it in patch notes or an in-client banner once the rotation is already live.
livePage.urfPara2: So a real "early warning" for URF isn't technically possible right now — that's not a gap on our end, it's that Riot never publishes this data anywhere in advance. The PBE/Live comparison above gives a real early signal for modes that have their own "hub file," like Arena or Swarm.
